speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness. To better assess your condition, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any night sweats or fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the combination of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and chronic cough over six months is very concerning. Given your recent release from prison, are you currently living in crowded conditions, and do you smoke or have anyone else in your household with a similar cough?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Tuberculosis. Given the classic B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), chronic cough, and significant risk factor of recent incarceration, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of active pulmonary tuberculosis. I am requesting a Chest_X-Ray and sputum AFB smear/culture to confirm the diagnosis.
